feed.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
feed.subtitle: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

entry.title: AI industry leaders call for development to slow down after recent safety concerns
entry.summary: After a string of security-related incidents involving AI agents and a high-profile resignation, AI industry leaders appear poised to slow down the pace of development to make sure it stays safe.

entry.title: Texas Rep. Greg Casar discusses bill to temporarily pause advanced AI development
entry.summary: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with U.S. Rep. Greg Casar, D-Texas, about his efforts to regulate artificial intelligence.

entry.title: U.K. and Irish politicians question Trump's comment on a unified Ireland
entry.summary: U.K. and Irish politicians on the left and the right are in rare agreement over President Trump's suggestion that Ireland and Northern Ireland reunite — he doesn't know what he's talking about.

entry.title: Morning news brief
entry.summary: Industry leaders call for AI development to slow down to ensure safety, Trump to campaign for GOP candidates ahead of midterms, Iranian officials say a meeting with the Gulf States has been postponed.

entry.title: New book highlights the people and institutions that have become Trump's enablers
entry.summary: NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks with author Jacob Weisberg about his new book, "Profiles in Cowardice: A Study of Collaboration in the Trump Era."

entry.title: Future of U.S. bases in Persian Gulf uncertain after Iranian attacks
entry.summary: Iran's attacks forced the U.S. to pull back many troops stationed in the Gulf, leaving the future of these bases in question.

entry.title: Forecast says families will spend more to heat their homes this winter
entry.summary: It's probably going to cost more to heat your home this winter. Forecasters say heating bills are likely to climb faster than overall inflation, despite what's expected to be a relatively mild winter.

entry.title: Research finds short bursts of vigorous movement are also beneficial for longevity
entry.summary: When it comes to longevity, lots of research has shown how much you move matters. But a new study finds your pace may also be key -- even if you fall far short of daily step goals.

entry.title: Local election officials are training to defend the midterms from interference
entry.summary: Hundreds of election officials from around the country are meeting to discuss how to defend the integrity of the midterm elections, including against interference by the federal government.federal government.

entry.title: NASA relocations could hinder agency's ability to build spacecraft
entry.summary: NASA has been moving engineers out of their labs as a way to reduce waste. But the moves may be limiting the agency's ability to make spacecraft.
